role: exploratory: do labelled examples in the prompt close the gap between hosted models and the fine-tuned specialist, and when should a smaller hosted model hand a turn to a larger one?
claim: Workflow v4 part A scored eight hosted models zero-shot: all were 10 to 20 points behind the fine-tuned specialist on the intent decision, and escalation from the specialist gained about ten points whatever the target's size. Two objections follow. First, a hosted model would normally be given examples. Second, v4 only paired the specialist with a hosted model, not a smaller hosted model with a larger one. Written after v4 part A was scored and before any request in this file was sent.
endpoint_rules: api_protocol.json and the workflow_v4_protocol.json request rules (prompt, codes, parsing, temperature 0, pinned hosts)
budget_note: The $20 project cap leaves about $3.7 after workflow v4. To fit, the few-shot part uses the first 150 of the 400 sessions (750 turns) and not every model gets every shot count. Saved replies are keyed by turn, so a later run on all 400 sessions would reuse them.

part_d_few_shot.examples: k training utterances per Banking77 label, the first k after a seeded shuffle of that label's training rows (seed 20261012; the Program 1 dev rows are excluded; no test or session item), and CLINC150 out-of-scope validation queries 10 to 13 with code 00. The examples are shuffled once and appended to the v4 current_only system prompt under the line 'Labelled examples (message => code):'.
part_d_few_shot.why_these: the best zero-shot model, the smallest, and the largest; the largest gets one shot count because it costs the most
part_d_few_shot.rows: each run alone, and as the escalation target for the encoder and the decoder at 10, 25, 40 and 60 percent of turns, against the same model's zero-shot answers on the same 150 sessions and the specialists alone on those sessions
part_d_few_shot.readout: stated before the run: examples close the gap if the few-shot model alone reaches the specialist alone on these sessions; the plateau the user asked about is reached if the model alone is at least as good as the best hybrid

part_e_model_pairs.calls: each small model answers all 2000 turns again in the v4 current_only form on a host that returns token log-probabilities. Its confidence in a turn is the product of the probabilities of every token it generated. These replies, not the v4 part A replies, are that model's answers in this part, so answer and confidence come from the same request.
part_e_model_pairs.targets: every other hosted model, using its saved v4 part A answers; no new call
part_e_model_pairs.rows: for each small model and target: the small model alone, the target alone, and the small model with its least confident 5, 10, 25, 40, 60 and 80 percent of turns replaced by the target's answer; controls are a random set (100 draws, seed 20261012) and the oracle set at each rate
metrics: AUROC of the small model's confidence for 'its turn decision is wrong'
session success and API cost per 1000 sessions at each rate (the small model's cost on every turn plus the target's on the escalated turns)
for each pair, the lowest rate at which the cascade is within one point of the target alone, and whether any rate beats both models
part_e_model_pairs.free_companion: artifacts/workflow-v4/pairs.json, computed from saved answers with no confidence signal: for all 56 ordered pairs, the share of turns the second model fixes and breaks, and oracle and random replacement

limits: One task and synthetic sessions. The few-shot part has 150 sessions, so its intervals are about plus or minus 8 points on session success. Token log-probabilities of a generated two-line answer are a coarse confidence.
